page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 x86_64 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, it provides 16 vCPUs distributed across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is configured at 128 GB, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The instance lacks local ephemeral storage and integrated GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating network-attached storage for persistent storage requirements.

Instruction set capabilities include AVX, AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI extensions. Benchmark testing indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with top-quartile results in stress-ng single-core execution, Geekbench single-core benchmarks, and text processing tasks. PassMark memory testing also ranks in the top quartile. Multi-core performance metrics, including Geekbench multi-core, PassMark CPU, and stress-ng multi-core scores, fall into the middle 50th percentile. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 49.58 GB/sec, while static web serving achieves 18.38 GB/sec.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio delivers high memory capacity per thread, offering high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require high physical core counts. The main architectural trade-off is the reliance on external network storage due to the absence of onboard NVMe drives. Recommended application fits include in-memory databases such as Redis, large caching tiers, enterprise text processing pipelines, and memory-intensive web applications.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz. It provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, paired with 128 GB of RAM to yield an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance operates on a KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. Benchmark evaluation demonstrates strong single-core CPU execution and PassMark memory performance, alongside average multi-core compute throughput and memory bandwidth scores. It maintains a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No local NVMe or SSD storage is attached, requiring remote block storage for data persistence, and no GPU accelerators are included. The hardware profile is qualitatively suited for memory-intensive enterprise tasks, such as in-memory databases, Redis caches, text processing, and data analytics environments that require a high memory-to-vCPU allocation.
